title: Hard Disk Activity widget goes out of bounds when first dragging it to the desktop from the widget picker
line: Widgets dragged onto the desktop now get tall enough for their contents, even when the pointer stays over them after the drop.
explanation: Right after a drop the pointer is still over the new widget, so it enters edit mode (handles shown). The widget's real size hints (Layout.preferredHeight) only arrive once its content has loaded, and the grid layout ignores size hint changes while an item is in edit mode and never retried, so the widget kept the 6-cell default height and its legend overflowed. The first drop usually escaped because loading took longer than the pointer stayed over it. Now the item remembers that a size hint change was skipped in edit mode and re-applies the hints when edit mode ends, unless its size changed meanwhile (a user resize is kept).

commits.message:
containmentlayoutmanager: apply size hints skipped in edit mode

A widget dropped on the desktop while hovered is in edit mode, and the
layout ignored the size hints it got then, leaving it too short for its
contents. Apply them when leaving edit mode unless the user resized it.

BUG: 524502

media.caption: Pure master, second drop still hovered: the second widget is created 164x132 and its Read row hangs below the background.
With the fix, same steps: the second widget is 164x180 like the first, legend inside.
Pure master after leaving edit mode (sweep tester): the second widget's legend still overflows.
With the fix after leaving edit mode: both widgets fit their contents.

review.text: The root cause diagnosis is sharp—the newly dropped widget enters hover edit mode before its asynchronous size hints arrive, and AppletsLayout ignores sizeHintsChanged while item->editMode() is true. However, deferring and re-emitting sizeHintsChanged inside ItemContainer fixes it at the wrong layer (coupling ItemContainer to AppletsLayout's internal edit-mode check and still leaving the widget visibly overflowing until edit mode closes), and recording m_sizeWhenSizeHintsSkipped lazily when size hints arrive can overwrite a user resize if a hint updates afterwards while still in edit mode.
changes: Fix the edit-mode size-hint handling in AppletsLayout (where the item->editMode() check lives) rather than coupling ItemContainer to AppletsLayout's internal policy—ideally by only ignoring sizeHintsChanged during an active user drag/resize so a newly dropped widget resizes immediately even while hovered, or by deferring inside AppletsLayout itself.

If keeping deferral until edit mode ends, record the item's size when entering edit mode (setEditMode(true)) rather than lazily on sizeHintsChanged, so a user resize followed by a subsequent size-hint change in the same edit session is still recognized as a user resize.
Ensure the verification screenshot and caption accurately distinguish still-hovered edit mode from post-edit-mode (after-1.png shows handles already mid-close).

reviews.text: The diagnosis fits the code: GridLayoutManager::adjustToItemSizeHints returns early while the item is in edit mode, and the hover edit mode right after a drop swallowed the applet's late preferredHeight for good. The third drop with the pointer moved away coming out right supports this. Remembering the skipped change and replaying it through the existing timer when edit mode ends, unless the size changed meanwhile, is small, sits in the right component and keeps user resizes (checked on the rig). It only ever grows items, like the existing logic. after-1 already shows the full height while the handles are visible, which the explanation doesn't quite account for (edit mode probably toggled once), but after-2 shows the state the reporter cares about.
